No, no, I haven't seen anything. No shadows or people standing in the corner or anything spooky like that. Oh, gosh, no. No, nothing like that. I mean, I watch those true crime shows on television where people find out their creepy landlord put a camera in the air vent or something, and sure, maybe that crosses your mind for half a second when you hear a voice out of nowhere, but... no. Like I was trying to say before, I really just think it's my own ears playing tricks on me, or... or my brain misfiring somehow. Well, I don't know if this is exactly what you mean by believing something most people wouldn't, because it wasn't like... a conspiracy theory or anything crazy like that. But there was this whole thing a little while back with my crafts. 

See, I do these resin crafts—coasters and little jewelry trays with dried flowers and gold flakes pressed into them. I was even looking up commercial warehouse spaces to rent for my "headquarters." Looking back now, I know how unrealistic that sounds, but at the time, you couldn't have told me otherwise. Oh, absolutely. That’s exactly what it was like during that whole resin craft thing I was just telling you about. I mean, at first I just felt so fired up, you know? I had this energy buzzing right under my skin, and I felt almost completely unstoppable about my craft business. But the hard part—and this is what makes me feel awful looking back on it—is that because I felt so unstoppable and I had all these massive plans, I had absolutely zero patience for anyone who wasn't on my exact wavelength. I mean, if he just asked a simple question about where the spatulas went after I rearranged the kitchen, or if he made one tiny little remark about how much space my molds were taking up on the dining table, I would just bite his head off.

I remember yelling at him, telling him he was trying to hold me back from my potential and ruin my business before it even started, just because he asked if I was ever coming to bed. I just felt this intense, irritable rush anytime he questioned my new house rules or my plans. It's embarrassing to think about now, how mean I was being, but at the time, I honestly felt like I was driving a racecar and he was throwing nails on the track. I just couldn't stand him—or anyone—being in my way.

I know there's no hidden microphone. It's just me, and the quiet, and that voice. I keep going over it and over it, pacing around the house, trying to find a completely normal, boring explanation for it, but I absolutely do not think anyone is spying on me or haunting me. I just want my head to be quiet again.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any thoughts that others might not have, like believing something is true that most people would say is not, even if you couldn’t prove it?\n\nPatient: Well, I don't know if this is exactly what you mean by believing something most people wouldn't, because it wasn't like... a conspiracy theory or anything crazy like that. But there was this whole thing a little while back with my crafts. \n\nSee, I do these resin crafts—coasters and little jewelry trays with dried flowers and gold flakes pressed into them. I started doing it at the kitchen table because, honestly, standing on the concrete at the warehouse for ten hours a day just absolutely ruins your feet and your lower back, and I needed something pretty and quiet to focus on when I got home. But anyway, a few months ago, I just... I got it in my head that I could turn my crafts into a real retirement business right away. And I don't mean just selling a few at a local church bazaar or putting them on the internet for pocket change. I mean, I was absolutely convinced that this was going to be a massive empire that would replace my income, and my husband's income, like, overnight. \n\nI remember I had all my little silicone molds spread out all over the dining room, and I was drawing these elaborate charts in a spiral notebook, calculating how we'd be completely set for life by the end of the year. I was so sure of it. I thought everyone would see I had figured out the perfect plan for our family. I was practically vibrating with how brilliant I thought I was. My husband tried to bring me back down to earth—he was standing there in his pajamas, pointing out that I’d only ever sold two coasters to my cousin and that the resin takes a full twenty-four hours just to cure, so making ten thousand of them a week was physically impossible. \n\nBut I wouldn't listen to a word he said. I just looked at him like he was the one who wasn't seeing reality. I literally believed I had unlocked some secret formula to wealth that nobody else was smart enough to see. I was ready to march into my supervisor's office at the warehouse the very next morning and quit on the spot because I just knew, without a shadow of a doubt, that my little kitchen table hobby was a million-dollar idea. I was even looking up commercial warehouse spaces to rent for my \"headquarters.\" Looking back now, I know how unrealistic that sounds, but at the time, you couldn't have told me otherwise. I just felt so incredibly important and smart, like I was the only one who had our whole future perfectly figured out.\n\nDoctor: When you believed your crafts would become a million-dollar business overnight, did you feel that this idea was so powerful or special that it could only have come to you, or did it feel more like a realistic business plan that just needed hard work?\n\nPatient: Well, you know, it definitely wasn't just about rolling up my sleeves and putting in the elbow grease.
